sections.h2: Where is Jonesboro, Arkansas, and how large is it?
sections.html:
Jonesboro is a city in northeastern Arkansas on Crowley's Ridge, and it is one of two county seats of Craighead County, along with Lake City. It covers about 80.7 square miles, which makes it the second-largest Arkansas city by land area after Little Rock.

The Census Bureau estimates 83,296 residents for 2025, up from 78,576 in 2020 and 55,515 in 2000, and Jonesboro is the fifth-most populous city in the state. The Jonesboro metro has about 139,440 people. Six public school districts operate inside the city limits, so the house you sell here may be zoned to Jonesboro, Valley View, Nettleton, Westside Consolidated, Bay or Brookland schools.

Growth like that keeps new construction and older neighborhoods side by side, and sellers in older parts of town often compete with new subdivisions on the edge.

Jonesboro was founded on February 19, 1859, and incorporated on February 15, 1883. It was named for state senator William A. Jones, and it was the original county seat when Craighead County was formed in 1859.

A fire in 1878 destroyed most of downtown. The present Craighead County Courthouse was finished in 1934. Railroads shaped the town's growth: the Cotton Belt line came through first, followed by the Frisco and Missouri Pacific lines. The oldest houses sit near downtown, and a seller there is competing against much newer construction elsewhere in town.

Arkansas State University is the largest individual employer in Jonesboro, directly and indirectly, and healthcare, agriculture, retail and manufacturing fill out the base. St. Bernards Regional Medical Center and NEA Baptist both operate in the city, and the region treats Jonesboro as its hospital hub.

Talk Business and Politics reported in July 2025 that Jonesboro housing units rose 8.2 percent over five years, from 46,939 to 50,801. The same article said the metro had 65,608 employed people in April 2025, up 1.8 percent from a year earlier, and a jobless rate of 3.1 percent. Mayor Harold Copenhaver has set a goal of passing 100,000 residents.

  • Arkansas State University and the NYIT College of Osteopathic Medicine campus on the A-State grounds bring students and staff who rent or buy nearby.
  • Food manufacturers came to the area decades ago for inexpensive water and electricity.
  • The Mall at Turtle Creek site sold in 2025 for about $4.85 million, with plans for an open-air mixed-use center.

Rising housing counts mean more competition for resale listings, but steady university and hospital jobs support a deep pool of renters, which helps landlords weighing a sale.

sections.h2: What weather and storm risks should Jonesboro homeowners know?
sections.html:
Jonesboro has a humid subtropical climate and a history of damaging tornadoes. The 1991 to 2020 normals show about 52 inches of precipitation a year over roughly 103 days, 3.9 inches of snow, a record high of 116 degrees and a record low of minus 18.

Tornadoes have hit hard. An F4 tornado on May 15 to 16, 1968, destroyed 164 homes and killed at least 34 people. Another F4 on May 27, 1973, killed three and injured 289. On March 28, 2020, an EF3 tornado with peak winds around 140 mph tore through the south and east sides of town shortly before 5 p.m., damaging homes, hangars at the airport and The Mall at Turtle Creek. At least 20 people were injured, and the National Weather Service reported no deaths.

For a seller, that history means buyers ask about roof age, storm shelters, insurance claims and permit records. If your house was repaired after the 2020 storm, gather the contractor paperwork before you list or accept an offer.

sections.h2: How does Jonesboro enforce property maintenance and vacant buildings?
sections.html:
Jonesboro's code enforcement office uses neighborhood sweeps and a boarding and securing ordinance to push owners to fix blighted property. The city announced monthly sweeps in July 2021, starting in the West End neighborhood, targeting tall grass, inoperative vehicles, unsanitary conditions and unlawful storage. Officers give warnings first and issue court citations on a second pass if the problem remains.

The boarding ordinance took effect January 2, 2020, with enforcement starting that April. Triggers include a vacant building with no utilities connected for 60 days. Broken doors and windows must be secured within seven days, and owners must repair, rehabilitate or demolish within six months of notice. Fines under the ordinance start at $100 per day, and failure to act can lead to abatement, condemnation or a citation.

  • Code enforcement phone: 870-933-4658.
  • An empty inherited house is the most common way a seller ends up under this ordinance.
  • Selling before the six-month window runs out moves the repair burden to a buyer.

sections.h2: What roads, transit and airport serve Jonesboro?
sections.html:
Jonesboro is crossed by AR 1, AR 18, US 49, US 63, US 78 and Interstate 555. Jonesboro Economical Transit (GOJO) runs four fixed bus routes plus paratransit, and Greyhound provides intercity service. The Jonesboro Municipal Airport is served by Southern Airways Express under the federal Essential Air Service program and was named the state's 2024 Airport of the Year.

Crowley's Ridge Parkway, Arkansas's first National Scenic Byway, passes through town. Whichever of these routes is closest to your house is worth naming when you describe the property to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do Craighead County property taxes work when you sell?
sections.html:
The Craighead County Collector collects property tax from the first business day of March through October 15 of the year after assessment. The collector's page said 2025 taxes could be paid without penalty through October 15, 2026, and that unpaid taxes after that date carry a 10 percent penalty, with interest on delinquent real estate taxes accruing daily.

A University of Arkansas Extension fact sheet noted that Craighead County voters were asked on November 3, 2026, whether to combine the treasurer and tax collector offices starting in January 2031. Ask the county about the outcome if you need to know which office will handle your bill in the future.

Arkansas reappraises real property on four-year cycles under Act 139 of 2023, and homestead taxable value can rise only 5 percent a year. A formal valuation appeal must be scheduled with the county board of equalization by the third Monday in August. The state's real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration, and the deed is recorded at the county clerk.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a Jonesboro house?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own or take a cash offer. A listing can bring a higher price when the house is updated and the timeline is flexible, but financing, inspections and appraisals can add weeks. A cash sale can close on the date you pick.

  • Storm-repaired or older houses: an as-is purchase removes the repair negotiation.
  • Vacant property: selling lets you avoid ongoing code citations.
  • Rental with tenants: ask whether the buyer will keep the lease.
  • Delinquent taxes: request a payoff figure from the Collector first.

faqs.q: How many people live in Jonesboro, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 83,296 residents for 2025, making Jonesboro the fifth-largest city in Arkansas.

faqs.q: Is Jonesboro in a tornado-prone area?
faqs.a: Yes. Jonesboro has had F4 tornadoes in 1968 and 1973 and an EF3 tornado on March 28, 2020. Buyers often ask about roof age and storm repairs.

faqs.q: When are Craighead County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due by October 15 of the year after assessment. After that date a 10 percent penalty applies, and delinquent real estate taxes accrue interest daily.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant, damaged house in Jonesboro?
faqs.a: Yes. Vacant buildings with no utilities for 60 days can trigger the city's boarding and securing rules, so many owners sell before the six-month repair window ends.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on deeds that convey real property for more than $100, according to the Department of Finance and Administration.
Six public districts operate inside the city: Jonesboro, Valley View, Nettleton, Westside Consolidated, Bay and Brookland.
